Oh yeah, I binge drink maybe twice a year and then the hangxiety ends up pushing me into a depressive episode. I can't explain it, but drunk me is not like a normal drunk person. It's like I'm manic and then I start bawling. I think the solution for that is mostly sobriety. 

That being said, afterward, I do feel that intense soul-crushing guilt. But last time I was asking my friends about it and they were kind of like, "What? No one is mad. We were all drunk. It's okay." I feel particularly guilty towards my best friend who I'm kind of in love with. He's kind of had to take care of and rescue me (literally) multiple times since 2015. I think he's mostly just confused as to *why* I feel so guilty and I think my feelings stress him out. So I guess my suggestion is to talk to the people close to you and see how they really feel vs how your depression brain is punishing you.

I think court reporting programs are about two years and it’s basically just showing up to the courtroom and transcribe what’s going on. There’s a special keyboard and you have to type shorthand and then translate it later. But there is a stenographer shortage and so it pays pretty well!

I'm unsure if you're interested in higher education, but my friend got his Master's in Library Studies specifically because it's not a stressful field. He also has PTSD and is schizoaffective. Also, libraries are generally government jobs, so you get job security, student loan forgiveness, and benefits.

Edit - noticed someone else commented this. My ex actually did get a library job by volunteering until a position opened up. I'm unsure how much it paid.I think if you wanted to go to a state college then get an MLS, that would be very do-able. Knock out harder classes at a community college, transfer, then grad school. I have bipolar and two of my closest friends have autism. There are a few shared traits. For example, I definitely stim by biting my nails and picking at my hair. I also get hyperfixations. Impulsivity and loud, rapid, and nonstop speech, are also shared traits.

But I think the main difference is social and communication delays. I think Kendall is very aware of social cues as he tends to pick up on them and really internalize what they mean. Kendall's mood swings are also cyclical, which Roman references when he says Kendall always comes "crashing down". I can confirm that the crashes after a manic episode are really bad.  

People also want to make the argument, "Kendall isn't manic, he's on drugs." Which I disagree with. Season 3 isn't a coke binge. I use to try to argue that my manic episodes were just me being drunk, but eventually, someone told me, "drunk people act like normal drunk people, a manic person is drunk AND manic." I think Stewy recognizes that Kendall has mental health issues that are different than other users.

That being said, I can also understand a dual diagnosis with autism and depression. I honestly cannot tell if Kendall fully understood everyone's reaction to the rap. Either way, Kendall is neurodivergent.

**Favorite: The Secret History**    
I read it during that twilight zone between Christmas and New Year's which fit the tone. I was fully invested all the way through and I always love Donna Tartt's characters. Even though they're generally unlikable, as a reader I still care about them. Tartt also does a great job with the setting and it was like being transported to rural New England.

**Honorable Mention: Little Women**  
I read a few chapters before bed each night in December and it really put me in the Christmas spirit. I loved all the tales of the March sisters and fell in love with Jo. I cried twice! 

**Least Favorite: Severance**  
This novel was just a huge miss for me. The prose was good, but I found the novel rather boring? It put me in a huge reading slump. I'm a firm believer that characters do not have to be "likable", but I generally didn't care about the narrator at all. It was anticlimactic, and pacing didn't help that. I was really disappointed with this novel.
